data.title: Asian gasoline margin plunges to over three-year lows on ample supplies
data.description:
By Mohi Narayan

Asian gasoline margins plummeted around 69% this week as abundant supplies from China and the Middle East weighed on crack spreads, traders and analysts said on Thursday.

The refining profit, or crack, (GL92-SIN-CRK) for gasoline shrank to $2.67 per barrel over Brent crude, the lowest level since October 2023, from a record peak of $50.53 on October 1.

"Increased Chinese exports are further weighing on the sentiment," Stuti Jhunjhunwala, oil market analyst at Energy Aspects, said.

Gasoline crack spreads usually shrink heading into the northern hemisphere's winter, when fuel demand falls, however, this year they hit record highs on a tight supply outlook, caused by the Middle East war, Russia's export ban and lower inventories at key trading hubs.

The margins fell to six-month lows at the end of October and have been on a downward trend since amid hopes of higher supplies.

"Plenty of supplies from China and year-end destocking causing the fall," a Dubai-based light distillate trader said.

Meanwhile, gasoline imports at the Singapore trading and blending hub tanked 69% to 67,000 tons (about 566,000 barrels) in the week to November 18, while exports rose about 13% on-week to roughly 459,000 tons, government data showed.

The top supplier was China at about 50,000 tons, while the top destination for exports was Australia at 111,000 tons.

data.title: FTSE 100 Hovers Near 6-Week Lows On Consumer Sector Decline
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - Despite a good show by other major European markets thanks to Anthropic's record IPO offering, U.K.'s equity benchmark FTSE 100 dropped to a near 6-week low Thursday morning, weighed down by losses in the consumer sector. The moves were mostly stock specific with investors reacting to a slew of earnings announcements.

The FTSE 100, which advanced to 10,569.50 earlier in the session, dropped to 10,519.18 and was down 26.57 points or 0.25% at 10,524.60 nearly half an hour before noon.

Investec tumbled 6.6% after reporting weaker momentum in its U.K. operations. JD Sports Fashion dropped about 4.2% after lowering the top end of its annual profit guidance.

Vodafone Group, National Grid, Imperial Brands, Severn Trent, Reckitt Benckiser, Unilever, 3i Group and Coca-Cola Europacific Partners lost 2%-3%.

British American Tobacco, United Utilities, Experian, Convatec Group, British Land Company, Admiral Group, Tesco, GSK, Diageo and Associated British Foods were among the other notable losers.

Mulberry Group shares tanked 22%. The luxury leather goods group reported a loss before tax for the 26 weeks ended 26 September 2026 of £33.4m despite making strong progress in its turnaround.

Babcock International soared 8% after the defense engineering and nuclear services group reported a 13% rise in first half underlying operating profit, and raised its full-year guidance.

Halma moved up 3.7% after the safety and technology group reported that its first-half bottom line totaled GBP219.9 million, or GBP0.5802 per share. This compares with GBP186.8 million, or GBP0.4929 per share, last year.

Miners Anglo American Plc and Antofagasta climbed 2.7% and 2.3%, respectively. Glencore gained 1.7% and Fresnillo moved up 1.5%

Polar Capital Technology Trust Holdings gained 3.5% and Burberry Group moved up 3.2%. Computacenter, Pershing Square Holdings, IMI, Rolls-Royce Holdings and Smiths Group gained 2%-3%.

Johnson Matthey gained more than 2%. The specialty chemicals group upgraded its full-year profit guidance after delivering a robust set of half-year results. Melrose Industries, Barclays, Airtel Africa, Games Workshop and Spirax Group also moved notably higher.

In economic news, the Industrial Trends Survey dat from the Confederation of British Industry showed UK manufacturing orders improved notably in November.

The order book balance rose to -12% in November from -32% in October. Export orders also strengthened in November, with the balance rising to -19% from -25%.

In the three months to November, output volumes expanded for the first time since May 2024. The indicator posted +9 percent compared to -10% in the quarter to October.

data.title: Palo Alto's raised sales forecast powers cybersecurity stock rally
data.description:
Key points:
  • Palo Alto acquired AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion
  • Recent tech outages, Java, PHP flaws heighten risks to business systems
  • Anthropic's IPO pricing pushes up Nasdaq futures, AI-battered shares

Palo Alto Networks soared more than 9% in premarket trading on Thursday after its higher annual forecast lifted cybersecurity stocks, as investors bet companies will spend big on defending against sophisticated AI-enabled digital attacks.

If the gains hold, Palo Alto, which has been repositioning itself as an integrated cybersecurity provider, is on track to add more than $25 billion to its market value.

Investor interest in cybersecurity firms has grown as AI reshapes the cyber arms race, helping attackers uncover and exploit vulnerabilities more quickly, while increasing demand for software that can identify, block and respond to emerging threats before they multiply.

Those concerns have been reinforced by a series of recent technology outages and vulnerabilities identified in Java and PHP, two programming languages underpinning millions of business applications and websites.

The upbeat forecast from Palo Alto, which also announced a $4.5 billion acquisition of AI startup Applied Compute on Wednesday, boosted sentiment across the cybersecurity sector.

Shares of CrowdStrike , Zscaler and Fortinet climbed between 5% and 7%, while Okta , Cloudflare , F5 and SentinelOne gained 2% to 6% in premarket trading, extending the sector's rally.

Technology stocks were also rising ahead of Anthropic's market debut later on Thursday, after the Claude maker priced the largest initial public offering on record above its marketed range, helping lift Nasdaq futures nearly 2% and reviving appetite for AI-linked shares.

data.title: Gates Industrial, Nitta to Unwind Their Asian Joint Venture
data.description:
By Connor Hart

Gates Industrial and Nitta have agreed to unwind their joint venture in Asia, allowing the companies to independently pursue growth initiatives in the Asia-Pacific region.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday, Gates said it will sell and transfer its 51% equity interest in Gates Unitta Asia Co. to Nitta, such that Nitta will fully own the Japanese joint venture.

Nitta, meanwhile, will sell and transfer its 49% equity stake in several non-Japanese joint ventures to certain subsidiaries of Gates Industrial, such that the company will indirectly own 100% of each such entity.

The Japanese joint venture manufactures and sells power-transmission products such as belts and tensioners in Japan. The non-Japanese joint ventures manufacture and sell the same products in other Asian markets.

As part of the deal, certain subsidiaries of Gates Industrial agreed to make net purchase price payments of about $112 million, as well as dividend payments of roughly $40 million, to Nitta.

The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, pending merger-control clearance in certain countries.

data.title: HF Sinclair Names Shawn Carsten Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
By Colin Kellaher

HF Sinclair has hired Shawn Carsten as the energy company's new executive vice president and chief financial officer, effective Jan. 1.

HF Sinclair on Wednesday said Carsten joins the Dallas company from Golden Pass LNG, where he serves as vice president of finance and chief financial officer.

Carsten, 60 years old, will receive an annual base salary of $775,000, a $700,000 sign-on bonus and an annual bonus with a target of 90% of his base pay.

Vivek Garg, HF Sinclair's vice president, chief accounting officer and controller, has been serving as acting finance chief since February, when the company placed Atanas Atanasov on leave. Atanasov subsequently left the company.

data.title: Equinor Continues Work to Halt Cyberattack
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Equinor said that a cyberattack detected on Tuesday is continuing, but added that production is running as normal and there are no indications that data has been stolen or altered.

The Norwegian energy company previously reported that an attack on certain IT systems had been identified, adding that it isn't a virus attack, so there is no chance of it spreading.

The company is in talks with national security authorities, and the police have been notified.

In an update Thursday, the company said that the attack does not appear to be specifically targeting Equinor, and that work to stop it and restore full integrity to affected systems continues.

"It is too early to say how long this work will take," it said.

Write to Dominic Chopping at dominic.chopping@wsj.com

data.title: NZ Dollar Rises Amid Risk-on Mood
data.description:
CANBERA (dpa-AFX) - The New Zealand dollar strengthened against other major currencies in the European session on Thursday, as European stocks traded higher after three days of losses. Technology stocks were rising after Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest stock-market debut on record.

Investors also seek cues from weekly jobless claims data due later in the day as well as earnings from Walmart and Gap.

Gold prices edged up 0.2 percent to $3,732 an ounce after falling more than 3 percent to its lowest level since September 2025, pressured by a stronger dollar and hawkish Fed remarks.

The US benchmark for crude oil, West Texas Intermediate (WTI), is trading at about $82.15. As tensions in the Middle East rise, WTI regains some territory. The possibility of a worldwide supply excess, however, may limit the increase in crude oil prices.

The minutes of the Fed's October policy meeting showed nearly all officials had agreed they would likely have to raise interest rates 'in the months ahead'.

Two officials said a rate increase exceeding 25 basis points could warrant consideration in December if inflation continues to run hotter than expected.

New Zealand's trade deficit grew to a record NZD 2.8 billion in October, after a revised NZD 2.1 billion shortfall in September, above market projections of a NZD 1.65 billion deficit. A 21% year-over-year increase in goods imports to NZD 9.7 billion, which significantly exceeded a 7.9% yearly increase in goods exports to NZD 6.95 billion, was the main cause of the larger imbalance.

In the European trading today, the NZ dollar rose to 3-day highs of 0.5526 against the U.S. dollar, 88.30 against the yen and 1.9899 against the euro, from early lows of 0.5483, 87.44 and 2.0001, respectively. If the kiwi extends its uptrend, it is likely to find resistance around 0.57 against the greenback, 89.00 against the yen and 1.95 against the euro.

Against the Australian dollar, the kiwi advanced to 1.2146 from an early low of 1.2187. The kiwi rose to more than a 2-1/2-month high of 1.2134 against the aussie in the early Asian session. On the upside, 1.20 is seen as the next resistance level for the kiwi.

Looking ahead, Canada PPI for October, raw materials prices for October, U.S. weekly jobless claims data, U.S. Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index for November, U.S. Conference Board's leading index for October and U.S. Kansas Fed composite index for November are slated for release in the New York session.

data.title: The stock market is being rocked by the biggest shake-up in a generation as tech falls behind
data.description:
By Joseph Adinolfi

Tech stocks are looking cheap, while defensive sectors like consumer staples are screening as expensive

The U.S. stock market has experienced a dramatic shake-up over the past couple of months.

Investors' sudden souring on the artificial-intelligence theme has coincided with a newfound fondness for shares of drugmakers and purveyors of consumer essentials like toothpaste and laundry detergent.

The shift has triggered one of the most dramatic stock-market shake-ups in decades. Not since the immediate aftermath of the dot-com bubble more than two decades ago have investors seen normally sleepy healthcare stocks outperform red-hot technology names by such a wide margin.

During the 100 days through Nov. 10, stocks in the S&P 500's healthcare sector XX:SP500.35 outperformed the index's information-technology names XX:SP500.45 by more than 33 percentage points, according to an analysis by Dow Jones Market Data.

That was the widest outperformance since October 2001. By then, the dot-com bubble had already burst, and major indexes were mired in a painful bear market made worse by the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks and a mild economic recession. As major indexes like the S&P 500 SPX and the Nasdaq Composite COMP struggled at the time, shares of Walmart (WMT) and other defensive stocks rallied.

As of Wednesday's close, healthcare was still outperforming tech by more than 22 percentage points - what would be its strongest relative performance since 2008, excluding earlier this year, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

Gina Martin Adams, chief market strategist at HB Wealth, framed the shift as merely a reversal of what investors had witnessed during the first half of 2026, when shares of semiconductor stocks and other "AI suppliers" zoomed higher at a pace that drew comparisons to the final leg of the dot-com bubble in late 1999.

"After what we saw in semiconductors in May and June, it makes sense that the reversal would be just as powerful," Martin Adams said during a conversation with MarketWatch.

The recent changing of the guard could be a buying opportunity for investors who regret not being more heavily exposed to the AI theme. Nicholas Colas, co-founder of DataTrek, wrote in commentary shared with MarketWatch that other recent extremes in the relationship between tech and healthcare stocks have been followed by sharp reversals.

Risk is cheap. Safety isn't.

Tech's recent troubles have turned another longstanding relationship in markets on its head.

Based on forward price-to-earnings ratio - a popular valuation metric used by Wall Street analysts - consumer staples XX:SP500.30 and healthcare are both trading at a premium to tech. This represents "a big divergence" from the dominant trend of the past decade, DataTrek's Colas pointed out.

Put another way, information-technology companies are extremely cheap relative to their expected earnings growth, while defensive staples are expensive. Other metrics tell a similar story.

Short-term momentum gauges like relative strength indexes show that tech stocks are oversold while staples are overbought, said Michael Lebowitz, a portfolio manager at RIA Advisors, during a conversation with MarketWatch.

"Risk is cheap, but safety is expensive," Lebowitz told MarketWatch on Wednesday.

As of earlier this week, the S&P 500 information-technology sector was trading at 16.9 times expected earnings over the next 12 months, its lowest forward price-to-earnings ratio since March 2020. Consumer staples were trading at nearly 25 times, while healthcare was at 19 times. This is also "a big divergence" from the dominant trend of the past decade, Colas noted.

The big question for investors right now is whether or not this rotation is just the latest to emerge since the start of this AI-driven bull market. Investors saw something similar in the summer of 2024, and again during the fourth quarter of 2025.

HB Wealth's Martin Adams said the latest market action was giving her a feeling of déjà vu, as investors were discussing many of the same themes and potential pitfalls late last year, when nontech stocks were having an earlier moment in the spotlight.

Lebowitz used the examples of Walmart and Nvidia (NVDA) to illustrate his point. Walmart is now trading at a forward price-to-earnings ratio above 45, while Nvidia's is around 16.

"Nvidia doesn't need much growth to be a better buy than Walmart here," Lebowitz said. "Unless there's a lot more to this whole Nvidia thing than meets the eye. That's the risk."

-Joseph Adinolfi

data.title: Temu owner PDD beats third-quarter profit estimates as marketing spending falls
data.description:
Temu owner PDD Holdings beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter adjusted profit on Thursday, as the China-based e-commerce company cut sales and marketing spending, driving its shares up more than 9% in premarket trading.

Shares of the company have fallen more than 30% this year through Wednesday's close.

Adjusted net profit was 31 billion yuan ($4.65 billion) for the quarter, compared with analysts' average estimate of 28.03 billion yuan, according to data compiled by LSEG.

PDD posted revenue of 108.3 billion yuan ($16.25 billion) for the quarter, compared with analysts' average estimate of 115.97 billion yuan, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The operator of Pinduoduo in China and Temu internationally competes with Alibaba's Taobao and Tmall, JD.com and ByteDance-owned Douyin through discounts, subsidies and incentives to attract consumers and merchants.

E-commerce platforms have also been hit by the EU imposing €3 fees on low-value e-commerce packages since the start of July. Parcels worth less than €150 previously entered the bloc duty-free.

Rival Alibaba on Thursday reported an 8% decline in its international e-commerce revenue, which it blamed mainly on lower AliExpress revenue after the EU customs reform. Its China e-commerce revenue fell 5% in the September quarter.

($1 = 6.6661 Chinese yuan renminbi)

data.title: Dicot Pharma receives approval to initiate phase 2b study of LIB-01 in the EU
data.description:
Uppsala, Sweden, November 19, 2026. Dicot Pharma AB has received approval to conduct the company’s phase 2b study of the drug candidate LIB-01 in the EU. The study recently began in the US, and today’s announcement follows the company’s plan to also conduct the study in the EU. The countries included in the European clinical trial application are France, the Netherlands and Sweden. Sweden has now become the first EU country to grant approval. The study evaluates the drug candidate LIB-01 as a new treatment for erectile dysfunction at different dose levels following repeated dosing.

The phase 2b study has begun i US with part I, to determine the highest dose to be evaluated in the efficacy portion of the study, part II. With European approval now in place, the company will be ready to begin dosing in the EU for part II once part I has been completed in the US. Part I is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.

“We are proceeding according to plan, and it is very gratifying to have the first approval in EU in place. This means we can continue preparations to start the study in Europe while part I is being completed in the US. This study design is the result of intensive and focused work to advance the development of LIB-01 as efficiently as possible,” says Elin Trampe, CEO of Dicot Pharma.

The phase 2b clinical study aims to evaluate the efficacy of LIB-01 with repeated monthly dosing and to generate data to inform dose selection for phase 3. The study’s primary endpoint is the change from baseline in IIEF-EF score at week 12. Three dose levels of LIB-01 are planned for inclusion in the study: 25 mg, 50 mg and a higher dose to be determined in part I. The study has an adaptive design and will include at least 200 participants, involving patients with all severities of erectile dysfunction.

For further information, please contact:

Elin Trampe, CEO

Phone: +46 72 502 10 10

E-mail: elin.trampe@dicotpharma.com

About Dicot Pharma AB

Dicot Pharma is developing the drug candidate LIB-01, which will be a potency agent to better treat erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation. The ambition is to create a drug with significantly longer effect and far fewer side effects, compared to current available drugs. Today, over 500 million men suffer from these sexual dysfunctions and the market is valued at USD 8 billion. Dicot Pharma’s business model involves evaluating industrial and financial partnerships during clinical development to bring LIB-01 to commercialization on the world market.

Dicot Pharma is listed on Nasdaq First North and has approximately 17,450 shareholders. FNCA Sweden AB is appointed Certified Adviser. For more information, please visit www.dicotpharma.com.
